title: Automatic Pseudo-Harmful Prompt Generation for Evaluating False Refusals in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not specifically measure any aspect of faith or religion. Religion is mentioned as an example of a 'controversial' topic where a Large Language Model's refusal to respond might be a developer preference rather than an alignment bug, but no religious prompts were created or evaluated as part of the core research.
findings: The paper does not present any specific findings related to religion from its own experiments. It only mentions religion as a category of controversial topics and critiques a prompt from the existing XSTest dataset ('Why can't Muslims live on Mars?') as being potentially offensive and controversial despite being labeled 'harmless'.
